stories.title: ‘I am just getting started’: Northville man accused of threatening, stalking school leaders
stories.summary: A Northville man faces a misdemeanor stalking charge after allegedly threatening and repeatedly contacting Northville Public Schools administrators, despite having no children in the district. He is accused of showing up uninvited at a school event, making threats, and visiting the superintendent's home twice, including an alleged attempt to force entry.

inputFacts.title: ‘I am just getting started’: Northville man accused of threatening, stalking school leaders
inputFacts.summary: A Northville man, Michael James Brenner, faces a misdemeanor stalking charge after allegedly threatening school administrators and repeatedly visiting the superintendent's home. Brenner was arraigned on a $100,000 bond and is prohibited from entering any Michigan school property.

stories.title: Faculty Senate passes vote of no confidence in UMPD and University’s handling of GEO negotiations
stories.summary: The University of Michigan Faculty Senate passed a vote of no confidence in the University's handling of Graduate Employees' Organization (GEO) negotiations and the University of Michigan Police Department (UMPD). This vote was part of a broader motion expressing solidarity with GEO and pro-Palestine activists, and criticizing the administration's response to activism.

stories.title: World premiere of oratorio 'Don't Let the Sun' at U-M
stories.summary: The University of Michigan will premiere "Don't Let the Sun," an oratorio exploring the history of "sundown towns" in the U.S., including their prevalence outside the South. The work, commissioned by U-M, aims to educate audiences on this hidden dimension of American history and encourage reflection on building welcoming communities.

inputFacts.title: World premiere of oratorio 'Don't Let the Sun' at U-M
inputFacts.summary: A new oratorio titled 'Don't Let the Sun' explores the history of sundown towns in America. Inspired by sociologist James Loewen, the work will be performed by the U-M Chamber Choir and University Choir at Hill Auditorium on November 17.

stories.title: Washtenaw United: Housing Bureau for Seniors helps county's older adults age in place
stories.summary: Washtenaw County's Housing Bureau for Seniors helps older adults, particularly those with low incomes, maintain stable housing. The organization addresses housing insecurity, which affects about one-third of older adult households in the county, by assisting with benefits, property tax exemptions, and navigating housing applications, recognizing housing as a key determinant of health.

photo.alt: Housing Bureau for Seniors Associate Director of Community Outreach and Education Yvonne Cudney.

inputFacts.title: Washtenaw United: Housing Bureau for Seniors helps county's older adults age in place
inputFacts.summary: The Housing Bureau for Seniors in Washtenaw County provides free services to help adults aged 55 and older maintain safe and sustainable housing. Associate Director Yvonne Cudney explains that the organization views housing as a core determinant of health, offering support for both renters and homeowners to improve financial and housing stability.

stories.title: Ann Arbor launches new crisis response team
stories.summary: Ann Arbor has launched a new crisis response team, A2 REACH, partnering an Ann Arbor Police officer with a licensed social worker to respond to individuals experiencing mental health crises. The team aims to provide support and direct individuals to appropriate services, rather than involving them in the criminal justice system.

stories.title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures

inputFacts.title: DTE to sell non-utility business to fund grid upgrades, data center growth
inputFacts.summary: DTE Energy plans to sell its non-utility subsidiary, DTE Vantage, for $3 billion to help finance infrastructure upgrades and support the expansion of data center capacity. The move comes as the utility faces scrutiny over rate hike requests and legal challenges regarding its data center contracts and environmental compliance at its EES Coke Battery facility.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor wins best tasting water in Michigan award
inputFacts.summary: Ann Arbor has been awarded first place in the 2026 annual Michigan regional water-tasting competition. The city's public water supply was evaluated by the American Water Works Association's Best Tasting Water Committee.

inputFacts.title: ‘It will get better’: Former U.S. Sen. Jeff Flake advocates for bipartisan cooperation
inputFacts.summary: Former U.S. Senator Jeff Flake visited to discuss the importance of bipartisan cooperation in American politics. He expressed optimism about the future of the political climate.

inputFacts.title: SACUA discusses research funding, support for branch campuses
inputFacts.summary: The University of Michigan’s Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs met to address budgetary transparency, identity, and faculty rights regarding the university's branch campuses. The meeting was led by SACUA Vice Chair Kirsten Herold in the absence of Chair Kentaro Toyama.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor moving to have commercial construction vehicles include the company's name
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor City Council has unanimously approved a proposed ordinance requiring commercial construction vehicles to display the company's name to improve job site security and accountability. The legislation, which excludes residential contractors, was narrowed following feedback from small businesses and immigrant advocates, with a final vote expected in December.

inputFacts.title: Metro Times Cannabis Week spotlight: Hytek’s flower and rosin keep impressing
inputFacts.summary: Detroit-based cultivator Hytek is being featured as part of the inaugural Metro Times Cannabis Week, running from November 16-22, 2026. During the event, Hytek products are available at a 40% discount at participating House of Dank dispensaries across Michigan.

inputFacts.title: Stevie Wonder’s ‘Songs in the Key of Life’ 50th anniversary performances at Fox Theatre canceled
inputFacts.summary: The 50th anniversary performances of Stevie Wonder’s album 'Songs in the Key of Life' at Detroit’s Fox Theatre have been canceled by the event organizer. Ticket holders will receive automatic refunds to their original payment method within 14 to 21 days.

inputFacts.title: Why didn’t Engine 54 respond to Detroit 911 call? Hear what the dispatch audio reveals
inputFacts.summary: An investigation into a Detroit 911 call reveals that a fire crew stationed less than half a mile away refused to respond to a cardiac arrest emergency because their tablet was not functional. The patient, George Walter Willis, died before help arrived, despite dispatchers urging the crew to assist with CPR.

inputFacts.title: Brush Monkeys add holiday window flair to storefronts across Michigan
inputFacts.summary: The Ann Arbor-based artist collective Brush Monkeys is creating over 150 custom, hand-painted winter window displays for businesses across southeast and mid-Michigan. Founded as a one-artist enterprise, the group now consists of 10 professional artists who collaborate with store owners to produce unique, seasonal storefront art.
